what: The section is pinned to the screen and the cards stack as a 3D pile (each card behind sits at z −120px · y −40px). For every 1.2 screens of scrolling per card, the front card drops 0.9 screens with power2.in and fades out over .25 starting at the .7 mark, while the cards behind each move one step forward (scrub .3). The pile tilts with the mouse up to rotationX 6° · rotationY 10° over .6s (power3), and the round badge turns a full 180° by the end

options.depth: z gap between back pages (px), default 120
options.offset: y gap between back pages (px, upward), default 40
options.per: Scroll used per card (multiple of screen height), default 1.2
options.tiltX: Max forward/back tilt with mouse (deg), default 6
options.tiltY: Max left-right tilt with the mouse (deg), default 10
options.spin: Angle in degrees the badge rotates to at the end, default 180
options.[data-fx-part=deck]: Tilting dummy panel (inside a parent with perspective). If none, the element itself
options.[data-fx-part=card]: Cards (in order from the front). Not applied when there are fewer than two
options.[data-fx-part=badge]: Round badge that spins to the end (only if present)

from.where: index.js card stack (original data-featured-stack — depth 120 · offset 40 · tilt 6/10 · scroll 1.2 · scrub .3 · 992px and up)

note: The original applies this only at 992px and up. The part likewise leaves the cards stacked vertically below 991px and under reduced motion, applying nothing. For the cards to stack on top of each other, the consuming css puts the cards in the same spot (position:absolute) and gives the dummy panel transform-style: preserve-3d — fx.css lays down the defaults.
